questions.hatred: What or whom do you hate?

origin.1: a small fishing village in the marshes
origin.2: a forest hamlet where neighbours lived a mile apart
origin.3: a loud river port that never sleeps
origin.4: the city slums, where the roofs lean toward each other
origin.5: a farmstead on a steep pasture among sheep and wind
origin.6: a roadside inn where every stranger was a friend for a night
origin.7: a mining town that smells of smoke and wet stone
origin.8: a market town at the crossing of two highways
origin.9: a border fortress where nothing ever happened until everything did
origin.10: a travelling camp that never had a place to call home

family.1: coopers who have made barrels for the whole quarter for three generations
family.2: tenant farmers who bend their backs on another man’s land and keep quiet
family.3: humble shopkeepers who count every copper twice
family.4: a lone mother who carried the whole household on her back
family.5: hunters and foresters who speak quieter than the wind
family.6: former soldiers who could never find their place at home
family.7: pedlars with a wagon full of other men’s goods and their own debts
family.8: gentle, devout folk who believed in better days
family.9: a stubborn grandfather and aunts who decided for everyone
family.10: strangers from a foundling house who became closer to me than blood

childhood.1: hungry, but full of warmth by the stove
childhood.2: quiet and monotonous, the days drawn out like wet rope
childhood.3: carefree, until someone had reason to frighten me
childhood.4: harsh, with the switch and the prayer always side by side
childhood.5: lonely, with imaginary friends and real bruises
childhood.6: loud, with a dozen cousins and one pot of stew for them all
childhood.7: like one long job: on my feet from first light
childhood.8: as happy as a childhood on the street can be
childhood.9: strange and bookish, for an old scribe taught me my letters
childhood.10: cut short too early, and I do not like to speak of it

turningPoint.1: the plague came and shut up half the street
turningPoint.2: our house burned down one night with everything we owned
turningPoint.3: a murder happened on the road, and someone saw that I had seen it
turningPoint.4: soldiers came to our parts and took everything edible and everyone young
turningPoint.5: a strange wanderer left me an object that others later came for
turningPoint.6: a casual game of dice ended in bloodshed
turningPoint.7: my patron died suddenly and the workshop went to the creditors
turningPoint.8: something nocturnal from the woods beyond the village came too close
turningPoint.9: a man in a cloak knocked at the door and spoke my name
turningPoint.10: the local lord decided that he needed our land more than we did

leftHome.1: my parents’ debts ate the land and the moneylender knew no mercy
leftHome.2: the gallows were already waiting for me there
leftHome.3: I was driven out for a truth spoken to the wrong person
leftHome.4: I was suffocating in one place; the village had no room for my dreams
leftHome.5: everything there reminded me of a loss
leftHome.6: someone had to earn, and there was no work at home
leftHome.7: those I had crossed were on my trail
leftHome.8: my parents sent me far away to be apprenticed
leftHome.9: one morning I woke with the feeling that the road was calling me
leftHome.10: the village began to whisper that something was wrong with me

friends.1: two scamps from the next yard, ready for any folly
friends.2: an old soldier who drinks for two and keeps silent for three
friends.3: a daring trader who knows the price of everything and everyone
friends.4: a loyal dog and a few people I let close only reluctantly
friends.5: old workshop mates scattered along the roads
friends.6: a wandering priest who never asks whether you deserve kindness
friends.7: a widow who keeps an alehouse and lends to those who have nothing
friends.8: a pack of street urchins who see everything
friends.9: a smuggler with a good heart and a bad reputation
friends.10: nobody, as yet; I only know how to rely on myself

loyalty.1: my family, whatever they may do
loyalty.2: the one who once held out a hand to me and demanded nothing
loyalty.3: my trade and the guild that fed me
loyalty.4: the lady of luck, for she is honest in her fickleness
loyalty.5: an old captain who still remembers my name
loyalty.6: my village and its land, though I left them behind
loyalty.7: a word given at a deathbed
loyalty.8: the god of war, not out of piety but out of gratitude
loyalty.9: my friends, but only those who walked through fire with me
loyalty.10: only myself, and I do not count it a flaw

hatred.1: moneylenders and all who profit from another’s misfortune
hatred.2: nobles who look at us like cattle
hatred.3: the darkness in the forest and whatever stirs in it
hatred.4: tax-men and guardsmen who take both their due and yours
hatred.6: strangers who look upon my land as plunder
hatred.7: witch-hunters and anyone looking for someone to burn
hatred.8: those who, with wine in them, raise a hand against the weaker
hatred.10: the very thought that my life is already decided for me

bestMemory.1: a summer evening on the riverbank when the whole family laughed
bestMemory.2: the first gift I bought with money I had earned myself
bestMemory.3: the harvest feast with music, dancing and warm ale
bestMemory.4: the moment a stranger saved my life for no reason at all
bestMemory.5: the night my grandfather showed me the stars and named each one
bestMemory.6: winning the village contest and being carried on shoulders
bestMemory.7: the smell of fresh bread and hands that broke it in half
bestMemory.8: my first journey along the road, when the whole world still lay ahead
bestMemory.9: a quiet talk by the fire with someone who is no longer here
bestMemory.10: the day I found out I was truly needed by someone

worstMemory.1: the sickness that took the dearest person among us
worstMemory.2: the fire I see every time I close my eyes
worstMemory.3: the night I had to keep silent when I should have shouted
worstMemory.4: the hungry winter when we shared the last crust
worstMemory.5: the execution in the square where I was brought to watch
worstMemory.6: the day someone I trusted turned away from me
worstMemory.7: a scream in the forest that no one answered
worstMemory.8: my father’s face when he lost everything we owned
worstMemory.9: the moment I had to choose whom to leave behind
worstMemory.10: the first blood on my hands and how quiet it grew afterwards

faith.1: I believe sincerely and pray each morning
faith.2: I whisper prayers only before battle or danger
faith.3: I honour the lady of luck: I touch wood and spit over my shoulder
faith.4: the gods abandoned me, and I return the favour
faith.5: I distrust priests, but I believe in signs and omens
faith.6: I keep old forest customs that I do not speak of aloud
faith.7: I believe in the god of war: a blade does not lie
faith.8: an amulet hangs at my neck that I never take off
faith.9: I doubt everything, yet dare not insult the gods
faith.10: I do not care who is above; what matters is who stands beside me

demeanor.1: fiery: I shout first and ask afterwards
demeanor.2: calm, and little throws me off balance
demeanor.3: prickly as a thornbush, yet soft beneath the thorns
demeanor.4: inquisitive: I must peer into every crack
demeanor.5: cautious to the point of suspicion
demeanor.6: cheerful even when there is no reason to be
demeanor.7: taciturn: words have to be pulled out of me with pincers
demeanor.8: bold and brazen, as if life were a game of dice
demeanor.9: meek, but with a long memory for slights
demeanor.10: changeable: my morning self and my evening self are near strangers

secret.1: I owe a moneylender more than I could ever repay.
secret.2: A crime is laid at my door that I never committed.
secret.3: I can read, though everyone thinks I cannot.
secret.4: Somewhere lives a kin of mine whom no one knows about.
secret.5: Dreams haunt me in which something speaks with my voice.
secret.6: I carry an object that belongs to someone dangerous.
secret.7: Someone who trusted me died because of my mistake.
secret.8: The name I go by is not my own.
secret.9: I am mortally afraid of water and hide it carefully.
secret.10: I secretly honour what law and temple forbid.

ambitionShort.1: To save enough to settle my debts
ambitionShort.2: To reach the nearest great city and not perish there
ambitionShort.3: To find a steady employer or patron
ambitionShort.4: To take revenge on one particular person
ambitionShort.5: To get a weapon and armour that will not fail
ambitionShort.6: To find someone who vanished without a trace
ambitionShort.7: To break free from another’s authority
ambitionShort.8: To earn a name known in every tavern
ambitionShort.9: To master a new craft or skill

ambitionLong.1: To open my own shop or workshop and leave it to my children
ambitionLong.2: To become a famed and respected hero
ambitionLong.3: To return home and find that I am awaited
ambitionLong.4: To win land and title, or at least an honest name
ambitionLong.5: To unravel the mystery that gives me no peace
ambitionLong.6: To destroy the evil that ravaged my homeland
ambitionLong.7: To gather enough gold never to depend on anyone again
ambitionLong.8: To build a family and a home where no one goes hungry
ambitionLong.9: To reach such mastery of my craft that others envy it
ambitionLong.10: To make peace with my past

sentences.leftHome: I had to leave home because {answer}.
